built: tools/assets/audio-fetch.sh: downloads Kenney impact/interface/rpg-audio/jingles, OGA creature-sfx/rpg-sfx/swishes and 7 RandomMind/Emma_MA tracks into assets-src/audio (77 MB, on disk). Safe to re-run (checked: second run only prints 'have ...'; .part files, curl retries).

tools/assets/audio-plan.mjs: the curated palette as data (37 sound ids, 105 variants, each with the file names, layers, processing and the measured evidence for the pick, plus the loudness table and runtime meta).

tools/assets/audio-build.sh (wrapper) + audio-build.mjs: mono 44.1 kHz OGG Vorbis q3 SFX (onset-trimmed <=1.5 ms lead, hard maxMs cap, raised-cosine tail fade, per-family loudness normalisation with a soft limiter, true peak <= -1.0 dBTP) and stereo OGG q2.5 music at -18 LUFS. It also regenerates src/audio/manifest.ts and licenses/audio.md from the plan, so the three cannot drift.

src/audio/manifest.ts (generated, plain data): SOUNDS {files,gain,family,priority,maxVoices,minIntervalMs,pitchVar} for all 37 ids in the brief (crown_tick chosen over throne_hit), MUSIC {file,loop,gain}, FAMILY_LEVELS. Paths look like 'audio/sfx/throw_1.ogg', relative to the site base.
src/audio/manifest.test.ts (extra, beside the manifest): 6 Vitest checks that every path exists and is OGG Vorbis, no orphan files, ids and metadata are sane, byte budgets hold. Passes.

licenses/audio.md: one row per (shipped file, source layer): source file, pack, author, CC0 1.0, download URL, 2026-09-30. 160 SFX rows + 5 music rows + a pack table. Licence checks: License.txt read inside all four Kenney zips (CC0); CC0 badge and author fetched from the OGA page of every pack/track.

Measurement tools: audio-lib.mjs (ffmpeg + a JS FFT, no npm deps), audio-measure.mjs, audio-music-probe.mjs, audio-verify.mjs (re-measures everything shipped), audio-reel.mjs (contact reel WAV, see needs_owner).
result.verified: "All numbers below come from tools/assets/audio-verify.mjs, which re-decodes the shipped files itself ('all checks passed'), and from npx vitest run src/audio (6/6). SFX: 105 files, all vorbis / mono / 44.1 kHz, longest 1.36 s, shortest 7 ms, max true peak -1.0 dBTP, leading silence <= 5 ms, no abrupt ends (last 4 ms at least 18 dB under peak). Music: all stereo, integrated -18.0 to -18.1 LUFS, true peak -2.9 to -8.4 dBTP (limit -1.5), decoded sample count equals source sample count for all five (no encoder padding in the decoded buffer). Loudness per family (momentary-max LUFS after encode, mean / target): sting -12.3 / -12, king -15.7 / -15, ability -18.8 / -15, building -19.0 / -16, critter -24.1 / -22, ui -26.3 / -21. Loud critter sounds (throw -22, land_hit -21) sit 7 dB under king and 10 dB under stings, as asked. Building/ability thuds are peak-limited (soft tanh limiter, max 4 dB) so they land 2-4 dB under target; 20 files report SHORT in the build log. Clicks/ticks of 7-60 ms (bite, no_ammo, ui_click, ui_hover) are normalised by peak (-10/-8/-4/-12 dBFS) because a 400 ms loudness window says nothing about them, hence their low mean M. Evidence for 'rise/fall' claims on the shipped files (f0 track or centroid sweep): hatch +8.5 st, king_respawn +5 st, kingscall +5 to +10 st, rampage +7 to +10 st, victory_sting +4.7 st, second_wind centroid 1.2>6.3 kHz and 4.7>8.7 kHz with the envelope peaking at the end, critter_die/king_down/capture_lost centroid falling, defeat_sting -9.7 st. Rejected on measurement: Kenney 8-bit jingles and confirmation/question tones (pitch 0.95-1.00, synthetic), back_003 (pitch 0.90 at 1.3 kHz, replaced by bookClose), spell_fire_04 (needs +14 dB of gain). Loop seams (measured on the decoded OGG, wrap step vs a typical sample step): battle 0.9x, crown 2.4x, menu 2.8x after a 10 ms de-click (the raw source loop had a 16.5x step). Crown loop: 88 beats cut from Battle at measured 104.93 bpm; onset-envelope correlation of the two crossfaded windows 0.82 at lag 0 after aligning the end by -31 ms (was 0.83 at a 29 ms offset before). Tempo method sanity check: it recovers whole beat counts for the native loops (Old Tower Inn 72.013 beats, Determined Pursuit 144.000).  What I could NOT verify without ears: whether the swishes read as soft pops rather than hiss; whether pitch-shifted cute_* squeaks sound cute rather than chipmunk; whether the pluck+swish arrow twang reads as a twang; that sax jingles read as a horn (no horn exists in the packs); whether the layered thud + grunt lines up naturally; that the bells are not harsh; how the tanh limiter sounds on thuds; that the Steel jingles are pleasant; whether Minstrel Dance is intense enough for battle and Battle for the Crown; and whether the 19 s / 22 s victory and defeat cuts end at a musical place. Pitch metric is unreliable on clips under ~60 ms. Not run: any playback in a browser (the engine is the next stage)."
fragile_or_unfinished: Variant counts deviate from the brief's 3-5: 22 rare/long sounds have only 2 variants (king_down, king_respawn, kingscall, recall, vortex, rampage, second_wind, freeze, capture, capture_lost, ui_confirm, crown_open, overtime) and both stings have 1. Cause: every Vorbis file carries a fixed ~3.5-4 KB header, so 105 tiny files are already 585 KB of the 600 KB SFX budget. Opus 64 kbps for the same 105 files measured 349 KB (-41%), which would allow 4-5 variants everywhere; I stayed on Vorbis as briefed. The studio-ai-audio.md research also recommends Opus.

Peak/loudness: thuds (turret_place, rampart, explode, stomp, freeze_2, ui_error_2) are 2-6 dB under their family target because of the crest factor; only a mid-frequency layer or a higher limiter depth would lift them, at the cost of more distortion.
vortex_1 (spell_fire_05) needs +12.6 dB of gain on a very quiet Vorbis source, so hiss is possible; unverified by ear.

Crown loop is beat-aligned by measurement only; the crossfade blends two beat-aligned but not phase-identical copies (waveform correlation 0.27), so a brief thickening around the loop point is possible.
Native loops menu and battle are used whole; menu got a 10 ms de-click at the head. battle is at 130 bpm and menu at 86.5, crown at 105 bpm, so any crossfade between tracks is not beat-matched.
victory (19 s) and defeat (22 s) are trimmed with 2.5 s and 4 s fades to fit the budget; original themes are 32 s and 45 s. Music is 2297 KB of 2600 KB; raising to q3 gives 2590 KB (too tight).
manifest.ts is GENERATED (header says so). Hand edits are overwritten by the next build; change audio-plan.mjs (META table holds priority/voices/interval/pitchVar).
manifest `gain` is 1 for every sound: levels are baked into the files, gain is only a trim on top.
No sound for throne_hit (no such sim event); crown_tick covers the tension tick. Sim events without an audio id in the brief: turretExpired, matchEnd uses the stings.
assets-src still holds Bard's Tale and Determined Pursuit (unused, 29 MB on disk); fetch script keeps them because assets-audio.md lists them.
tsc has errors in src/ai (missing ./match, ./profiles); none in src/audio.
needs_owner: One listening pass (about 5 minutes): open .cache/audio/contact-reel.wav (89 s, every SFX variant in manifest order, 0.35 s between variants; timestamps in .cache/audio/contact-reel.txt) and the five files in public/audio/music. Regenerate any time with node tools/assets/audio-reel.mjs. Things to listen for are in the 'could not verify' list in the verified field. Nothing else needs an account or money.
result.notes_for_lead: "Machine notes from this run (RAM was 0.7 to 2 GB free the whole time, owner's browser open): I kept every job to one process at a time, put all raw audio, temp files and reports under assets-src/ and .cache/ (disk), never /tmp, and all measurement is dependency-free Node + ffmpeg. numpy/scipy are not installed here, so instead of adding a Python env (uv would have cached hundreds of MB) I wrote a 40-line FFT in JS; it takes ~0.3 s per clip. Peak RSS of any of my processes stayed under ~250 MB (music decode is 20 MB of float32). OpenGameArt downloaded at ~6 KB/s for the first two minutes then at full speed, so fetch runs in the background with .part files and resumes safely. The 'needs money' paths were avoided: AI audio (SA3/ElevenLabs) was not needed because CC0 packs cover all 37 ids; the only real gap was a horn, filled by the sampled Sax jingles, and a shield ring, filled by plate/bong impacts. Suggested additions to STUDIO.md (I do not own it): 'ffmpeg loudnorm/ebur128 and a JS FFT replace a Python audio stack', 'Vorbis has ~3.5-4 KB fixed header per file, Opus ~1.5 KB, so many tiny SFX files favour Opus or sprites', and 'background long downloads, poll with a bounded until-loop'. Decision for you: switch SFX to Opus (349 KB vs 596 KB) and use the saved ~250 KB for 3-5 variants everywhere; Safari support for Ogg Opus should be checked first (research says Vorbis in Ogg needs Safari 18.4). Engine notes: pick a random file avoiding the last one; playbackRate = 2^(±pitchVar/12); music loops can use the whole file as the loop (menu, battle, crown are sample-exact loops; victory/defeat are one-shots); Chromium decode of Vorbis is sample-exact per studio-ai-audio.md. Rebuild everything with tools/assets/audio-fetch.sh then tools/assets/audio-build.sh (about 90 s), check with node tools/assets/audio-verify.mjs. I did not touch package.json, STUDIO.md or any file outside my ownership except adding src/audio/manifest.test.ts."
